FOREWORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Organic Chemicals (Miscellaneous) Sectional Commi(tce had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. This standard wtis first published in 1975. The Sectional Committee responsible for the standard felt that the standard should be revised with a view to update it in accordance with technology. In this revision the requirements of moisture content and equivalent mass have test method for purity has been changed. A more accurate CC method has been incorporated impurities can.ako be determined. preparation of this the advancement in been modified. The through which the

The largest use of diethanoltirnine is in the scrubbing processed for the removal of C02 and HJ from natural gas and other gases. Huge quantity of the material is used in the manufacture of morpholine, surface active agents, textile specialities, herbicides and petro-demulsifiers. It is..also extensively used as an intermediate for rubber chemicals; as an emulsi tier and dispersing agent in various agricultural chemicals, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals; in the production of lubricants for the textile industries; as humectant and softening agents; and in organic synthesis. For the preparation of this standard considerable assistance has been drawn from British Pharmacopoeia Vol I, 1988 and US Pharmacopoeia, 1995. Assistance has also been sought from Hydro Carbon Processing and Industrial Engg. (Vol 59, No. 4 -- Control DEA degradation). For the purpose of deciding whether observed or calculated, expressing IS 2:1960 `Rules for rounding off the rounded off value should be the a particular requirement of this standard the result of a test or analysis, shall be numerical values (revised)'. The number same as that of the specified value in this is complied with, the final value, rounded off in accordance with of significant places retained in standard.

Indian Standard DIETHANOLAMINE -- SPECIFICATION (First Revision)
1 SCOPE This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for diethanolamine. 2 NORMATIVE REFERENCES 3 REQUIREMENTS 3.1 Description The material shall mainly consist of diethanolamine [HN (CHXCHXOH)X]and may contain small amounts of monoethanolamine and triethanolamine. It shall be a clear liquid with a slight characteristic odour. 3.2 Miscibility It shall be miscible with water and with ethanol (96%) in all volumes and slightly soluble in ether. 3.3 The material shall also comply with the requirements given in Table 1. 4 PACKING 4.1 Packing The material drums. 4.2 Marking Each container shall be securely closed and shall bear legibly the following information: a) b) Name of the material; Net mass of the material; shall be packed in air-tight mild steel AND MARKING

ANNEX B [Table 1, S1No. (ii)]
DETERMINATION B-1 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD Moisture is determined by the Karl Fischer Method using electrometric end-point. B-2 PROCEDURE Transfer 75 ml of methanol to the titration flask. Add OF MOISTURE CONTENT

15 ml of glacial acetic acid and titrate with the Fischer reagent to the end-point. To the titrated liquid quickly add an accurately weighed quantity of the material, stir vigorously and again titrate with the reagent. Determine the moisture content of the resulting solution by the procedure given in IS 2362.

ANNEX D [Table 1, S1No. (iv) and (v)]
DETERMINATION D-1 GENERAL Two methods have been prescribed nation of diethanolamine. D-2 METHOD D-2.1 Reagents D-2.1.1 Su@/zuric Acid 3N. D-2.L2 0.1 N. D-2.1.3 Standard Sodium Arsenite Solution -- 0.1 N. Dissolve 5 g of arsenic trioxide in a mixture of 20 ml of sodium hydroxide solution and 20 ml of water, dilute to 400 ml with water and add dilute hydrochloric acid until the solution is neutral to litmus paper. Dissolve 4 g of sodium bicarbonate in the solution and dilute to 1000 ml with water. Ascertain its exact strength by diluting 25 ml with 50 ml of water, adding 5 g of sodium bicarbonate, and titrating with 0.1 N iodine, using starch solution as indicator. D-2.1.4 Standard iodine Solution Periodic Acid Solution 1 for the determiOF DIETHANOLAMINE D-2.2 Procedure Add 0.12 g of the sample to 50 ml of sulphuric acid contained in a .500-ml glass-stoppered conical flask. To this add while swirling exactly 35 ml of periodic acid solution and let it stand for exactly 1 minute. This time should start from the last drop of periodate addition. Neutralize the acid completely and carefully by adding solid sodium bicarbonate. Add from a burette, 50 ml of standard sodium arsenite solution, allow to stand for 10 minutes with occasional stirring and titrate with standard iodine solution using starch indicator till the first appearance of blue end-point. Similarly carry out a blank titration. D-2.3.1 The percentage of monoethanolamine in the sample shall be determined by the same procedure as prescribed in A-5ofIS7910 by using 1 g of the sample in 10 ml of the liquid. D-3 METHOD II -- GC METHOD D-3.1 Outline of the Method About 3 g of the sample is dissolved in 100 ml of distilled water and 0.2 ml of the sample is introduced into the separating column of a gas chromatography by means of a syringe. The vaporized sample is swept through a packed column by a flow of carrier gasand as each component emerges, it is detected by flame ionization detector and recorded as a peak in a chromatogram. Under the operating conditions the impurities are identified by their relative retentions and are determined from their peak areas taking their respective response factors into consideration. D-3.2 Column - Packed Material Length OD Packing material D-3.3 Reagents D-3.3.1 Monoethanolamine D-3.3.2 Pure diethanolamine D-3.3.3 Pure triethanolamine - Purity, 99 percent. -99 percent. ANNEX E [Table 1, S1 No. (vii)]
DETERMINATION E-1 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD The material is slowly cooled to determine its crystallizing point by observation of the temperature during crystallization under prescribed conditions. E-2 APPARATUS The crystallizing point apparatus shall be as shown in Fig. 4. A thick glass tube of'nominal size 100x 25 mm is placed inside a large glass test tube of nominal size 150 x 50 mm. The latter tube is flanged so that it may be supported central] y by the metal cover plate. E-2.1 The wider tube is weighed with lead shots or similar material and the inner tube is closed by means of a cork, which carries a glass stirrer and through its centre a standard thermometer. The thermometer is so fixed in the cork that the thernlometer's immersion mark is in level with the top of the cork and if the thermometer"has a contraction chamber, the distance from the bottom of the bulb to the top of the contraction chamber shall not be more Lhan 35 mm. E-2.2 The wider tube is supported in a 1 000-ml tallform beaker filled with cooling liquid to within 20 mm of the top. A thermometer for the cooling bath passes through a hole in the cover plate and is held by a rubber ring. OF CRYSTALLIZING E-2.3 Thermometer Conforming be used.
NOTE

POINT

to the Schedule Mark 22 of IS 4825 shall

-- Any thermometer

of

convenient range and similar

rcqulrcrnents and accuracy may be used.

E-2.3.1 The thermometer shall bear a certificate from the National Physical Laboratory, New Delhi or any other institution authorized by the Government of India to issue such a certificate. E-3 PROCEDURE Take about 25 ml of the sample in the inner tube of the crystallizing point apparatus, immerse the thermometer and start stirring. Cool in water-bath adding ice to it to bring down the temperature. The temperature drop should be regulated so that the.rate of cooling is about 2�C below the expected crystallization point, seeding crystal is introduced, if necessary, with stirring. At the point of crystallization, temperature will rise and then remain steady for the duration of crystallization. This steady temperature represents the crystallization point. Care should be taken to ensure that the apparatus is clean and dry betore use.

ANNEX F (Clause 5)
SAMPLING F-1 GENERAL SAMPLING REQUIREMENTS FOR F-2.3.1 These containers shall be selected at random from the lot and to ensure the randomness of selection, random number tables shall be used (see IS 4905). In case random number tables are not available, the following procedure may be adopted: Arrange all the containers in the lot in a systematic manner and starting from any container, count them as 1, 2, 3,.., up to r and so on, r being the integral part of Nln (N being the lot size and n the number of containers to be selected). Every rth container thus counted shall be withdrawn to constitute the sample. F-3 INDIVIDUAL SAMP-LE SAMPLES AND COMPOSITE

F-1.l Samples shall be taken in a protected place not exposed to damp air, dust or soot. F-1.2 The sampling instrument shall be clean and dry. F-1.3 Precautions shall be taken to protect the samples, the material being sampled, the sampling instruments and the containers for samples from adventitious contamination. F-1.4 To draw a representative sample, the contents of each container selected for sampling shall be mixed as thoroughly as possible by suitable means. F-1.5 The samples shall be placed in suitable, clean, dry and airtight glass bottles or other suitable containers on which the material has no action. F-1.6 The sample containers shall be of such a size that they are almost three-fourths tilled by the sample. F-1.7 Each sample container shall be sealed airtight after filling, and marked with full details of sampling, the date of sampling and details given under 4.2. F-2 SCALE F-2.1 Lot All the containers in a single consignment of the tnaterial drawn from a single batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot. If a consignment is declared to consist of different batches of manufacture the batches shall be marked separately and the groups of containers in each hatch shall constitute separate lots. F-2.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the material in any lot to the requirements of this -specification, samples shall be tested for each lot separately. F-2.3 The number of containers to be selected from the lot shall depend on the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with Table 2. Table 2 Number of Containers to be Selected from Lots of Different Sizes
(Ckfu.w

F-3.1 From each of the containers selected according to F-2.3, a representative portion of the material, about 300 ml in volume, shall be drawn. These samples shall constitute individual samples. F-3.2 From each of these individual portions (F-3.1), an equal quantity of the material shall be taken and thoroughly mixed to constitute a composite sample not less than 1 000 ml in volume. The composite sample shall be divided into three parts, one for the purchaser, one for the supplier and the third for the referee. F-3.3 Referee Sample The referee sample consists of the composite sample marked for this purpose, and shall bear the seals of both the purchaser and the supplier. It shall be kept at a place agreed to between the two and shall be used in case of dispute. F-4 NUMBER OF TESTS

OF SAMPLING

F-4.1 Tests for the determination of all the characteristics given in Table 1 shall be carried out on the composite sample. F-5 CRITERIA OF CONFORMITY
